text: RESULTS: Spirometry: Forced Vital Capacity (FVC): 3.1 L, Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 second (FEV1): 1.9 L, FEV1/FVC Ratio: 0.61 (reduced); Chest X-Ray: Hyperinflated lungs, flattened diaphragms, no acute infiltrates or obvious masses.

speaker: Doctor
text: The spirometry results showing a reduced FEV1/FVC ratio and the X-ray findings of hyperinflation are classic signs of obstructive lung disease. Do you notice your symptoms worsening during winter months or when exposed to cold air? Additionally, have you ever been diagnosed with asthma or experienced episodes of wheezing in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, I definitely notice my breathing gets much harder when the weather turns cold or during winter. I was diagnosed with COPD five years ago, and I do wheeze quite a bit, especially when I try to play basketball.

speaker: Doctor
